fixtures.title: Decision: a single repository for backend services
fixtures.content: Northwind uses a single repository for backend services. separate repositories per service was considered and rejected, because shared tooling and atomic cross-service changes outweighed the build complexity.

fixtures.title: Decision: relational storage as the default
fixtures.content: Northwind uses relational storage as the default. document storage as the default was considered and rejected, because most access patterns turned out to be relational once reporting was included.

fixtures.title: Decision: asynchronous fulfilment
fixtures.content: Northwind uses asynchronous fulfilment. synchronous fulfilment inside checkout was considered and rejected, because checkout latency mattered more than immediate confirmation.

fixtures.title: Decision: running our own search cluster
fixtures.content: Northwind uses running our own search cluster. a hosted search product was considered and rejected, because per-query cost at catalogue scale was prohibitive on the hosted option.

fixtures.title: Decision: rate limiting at the edge
fixtures.content: Northwind uses rate limiting at the edge. rate limiting in each service was considered and rejected, because a single enforcement point was easier to reason about during incidents.

fixtures.title: Decision: hand-written SQL in the data layer
fixtures.content: Northwind uses hand-written SQL in the data layer. a full ORM was considered and rejected, because query plans were too important to leave implicit.

fixtures.title: Decision: a base-currency ledger
fixtures.content: Northwind uses a base-currency ledger. a multi-currency ledger was considered and rejected, because reconciliation was simpler with conversion at the boundary.

fixtures.title: Decision: event sourcing for orders only
fixtures.content: Northwind uses event sourcing for orders only. event sourcing everywhere was considered and rejected, because the audit requirement applied to orders and nowhere else.

fixtures.title: Decision: blue-green deployment for stateless services
fixtures.content: Northwind uses blue-green deployment for stateless services. rolling deployment everywhere was considered and rejected, because instant rollback was worth the doubled capacity during a release.

fixtures.title: Decision: managed PostgreSQL
fixtures.content: Northwind uses managed PostgreSQL. self-managed PostgreSQL on EC2 was considered and rejected, because the operational burden was not where the team could add value.

fixtures.title: Decision: gRPC for internal calls
fixtures.content: Northwind uses gRPC for internal calls. REST for internal calls was considered and rejected, because schema enforcement across teams mattered more than curl-ability.

fixtures.title: Decision: buying a feature flag service
fixtures.content: Northwind uses buying a feature flag service. extending the homegrown table was considered and rejected, because targeting and audit requirements had outgrown the internal version.

fixtures.title: Decision: one datastore per service
fixtures.content: Northwind uses one datastore per service. a shared datastore across services was considered and rejected, because shared schemas had repeatedly coupled unrelated releases.

fixtures.title: Decision: storing all timestamps in UTC
fixtures.content: Northwind uses storing all timestamps in UTC. storing local time with an offset was considered and rejected, because reporting boundaries had already been misstated twice.
alternatives: storing local time with an offset

fixtures.title: Decision: caller-supplied idempotency keys on payments
fixtures.content: Northwind uses caller-supplied idempotency keys on payments. server-side deduplication windows was considered and rejected, because the duplicate charge incident made caller intent the safer signal.

fixtures.title: Decision: read replicas for reporting
fixtures.content: Northwind uses read replicas for reporting. reporting against the primary was considered and rejected, because nightly extracts were competing with checkout traffic.

fixtures.title: Decision: soft deletion for customer records
fixtures.content: Northwind uses soft deletion for customer records. hard deletion was considered and rejected, because erasure requirements needed a deliberate, auditable path rather than a cascade.

fixtures.title: Decision: versioning the partner API by URL
fixtures.content: Northwind uses versioning the partner API by URL. versioning by header was considered and rejected, because partners found the URL form easier to pin and to debug.

fixtures.title: Decision: a central configuration service
fixtures.content: Northwind uses a central configuration service. per-service environment variables was considered and rejected, because changing a value across the estate had required a deploy per service.

fixtures.title: Decision: strongly consistent inventory reads
fixtures.content: Northwind uses strongly consistent inventory reads. eventually consistent inventory reads was considered and rejected, because overselling cost more than the added read latency.
